Situation.Name: The Old Machine Learns
Situation.Setting: A dim home workshop at night. A 1981 Radio Shack TRS-80 Color Computer sits on the desk in the foreground, keyboard toward the viewer, with a Commodore 1702 monitor beside it showing a green screen. The room behind is out of focus, lit by cyan and magenta neon.
Situation.Camera: Mid-shot, slightly low angle across the desk. The computer fills the lower third of the frame in sharp focus; the character sits behind it, off-centre to the right, looking at the CRT.

CharacterPose.Expression: Quiet delight, eyebrows slightly raised, half-smile lit green by the screen
CharacterPose.BodyPosition: Seated behind the desk, leaning in toward the machine
CharacterPose.Gesture: One hand resting on the CoCo's keyboard, the other holding a twenty-sided die between finger and thumb

Article.Name: Stacey's CoCo 1
Article.Description: The exact Radio Shack TRS-80 Color Computer in the reference photo: a wide, low silver-grey case, scuffed and worn from forty-five years of use, with a black recessed keyboard well, small yellowed chiclet keys with dark legends, a red reset key at the top right, a Radio Shack badge with the red, green and blue stripe above the keys, and ventilation slots along the sides. Do not modernise it, clean it, or change its proportions.
Article.Application: Foreground, keyboard toward the viewer, sharp focus, its worn plastic catching the green screen light
Article.SymbolicMeaning: The whole mechanism, small enough to see, on a machine that cannot hide anything

Article.Name: Commodore 1702 monitor
Article.Description: The exact monitor in the reference photo: a beige Commodore 1702 video monitor with a deep, rounded CRT face set well back inside a dark rectangular bezel, a lighter frame around it, a row of small control knobs and a brand strip along the bottom edge. Its screen is the CoCo's own picture: a bright green raster with a dark green tint at the edges, showing rows of soft, out-of-focus text; no readable words or letters. Do not modernise the monitor or change its proportions.
Article.Application: On the desk beside the computer, angled toward the character, the main light source
Article.SymbolicMeaning: The output, seen but not read

Article.Name: Twenty-sided die
Article.Description: A translucent amber d20 catching the neon
Article.Application: Held lightly in the character's free hand
Article.SymbolicMeaning: The roll that picks the next word

Environment.Name: Workshop shelves
Environment.Description: Out-of-focus shelves with old hardware, tools and cables, neon reflections. No posters, no signs, no labels.

Environment.Name: Coiled cables
Environment.Description: A few old grey cables on the desk

Environment.Name: Plain coffee mug
Environment.Description: A plain dark ceramic mug with nothing printed on it
Environment.Application: On the desk, edge of frame

KeyDetails: The computer and the monitor are unmistakably the machines from their reference photos, not generic retro equipment
The CRT's text is a soft green glow, deliberately unreadable
Green screen light on her face and hands against cyan and magenta from the room
NO WORDS ANYWHERE IN THE IMAGE: no signs, posters, slogans, neon lettering, book titles, mug slogans, labels or captions. The only text-like element is the unreadable glow on the CRT.
No smartwatch, no modern devices, no phone; the only technology in focus is the 1981 machine and its monitor
Situation.LightingFocus: Green phosphor glow from the CRT on the character and the keyboard; neon rim light separates her from the dark room
